title: Obadiah
summary: Obadiah is a biblical book focused on Edom's pride, judgment against the nations, and Zion's restoration.
historical_context: Obadiah announces judgment on Edom and widens the vision to the day of the Lord.
ancient_near_east_context: Obadiah belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Obadiah should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Obadiah as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Minor Prophets, book 4 of 12, Obadiah contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting Edom's pride, judgment against the nations, and Zion's restoration to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Obadiah as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Obadiah uses prophecy, poetry within Minor Prophets, book 4 of 12 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Obadiah helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional prophetic attribution to the named prophet
Many scholars recognize collection and editorial shaping
date_ranges: 8th-5th centuries BCE, depending on the prophet
Final forms often reflect later collection and editing
original_audience: Israel and Judah under covenant accountability before and after exile
historical_setting: Assyrian, Babylonian, and post-exilic settings across the prophetic corpus
canonical_role: Obadiah anchors Edom's pride, judgment against the nations, and Zion's restoration within Minor Prophets, book 4 of 12 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How to read prophetic poetry, irony, and symbolic action

related_objects.notes: Edom is the direct target of the oracle.

The oracle widens to the day of the Lord among the nations.
The book emphasizes justice against violence toward kin.
Judgment on Edom is paired with restoration for Zion.
